And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. It would ordinarily be a tall task. They have been to two Super Bowls in the last five years, and they have one Lombardi. They're a perennial playoff team. But this week, Jalen Hurts is out, and others are likely to join him. The Panthers are rested, and the Eagles are coming back from London after a tough loss. The Panthers also seem to be on the rise, while the Eagles are decidedly not. Does this mean the Panthers will win? Here's what the Panthers on SI staff believes. Russell Baxter: Panthers 27, Eagles 23 Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) throws the ball during the fourth quarter | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Carolina had some extra time to get ready for this clash of defending division champions. Ejiro Evero's defense is still shorthanded, but the Eagles are in the midst of a three-game losing streak. Philadelphia's defensive line could make things difficult for Bryce Young. Carolina had some extra time to get ready for this clash of defending division champions. Ejiro Evero's defense is still shorthanded, but the Eagles are in the midst of a three-game losing streak. Philadelphia's defensive line could make things difficult for Bryce Young. Nick Sirianni's team, which will be without quarterback Jalen Hurts, has been outscored a combined 66-23 in the second half this season and will struggle to close out the surging Panthers. Mark Livingston: Panthers 27, Eagles 20 Going into Philadelphia is never easy, but this is a game the Panthers should win. The Eagles have lost three straight and now have to turn to Tanner McKee with Jalen Hurts out. Carolina is coming off the bye, the offense has been playing well, and I think Bryce Young makes enough plays for the Panthers to leave Philadelphia with a big road win. Zach Roberts: Panthers 31, Eagles 17 Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (26) is helped off the field | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Eagles' defense has struggled against the pass, allowing the seventh-most passing yards per game. Bryce Young has taken on the defenses ranked first and sixth in passing yards allowed and shredded them both, so the Panthers, who are getting healthier, should have no issues moving the ball. The Eagles' defense has struggled against the pass, allowing the seventh-most passing yards per game. Bryce Young has taken on the defenses ranked first and sixth in passing yards allowed and shredded them both, so the Panthers, who are getting healthier, should have no issues moving the ball. The Eagles' offense, meanwhile, is without Jalen Hurts. Saquon Barkley probably won't play. Will Shipley is out. Devonta Smith might miss Week 6, too. The Eagles just lost Lane Johnson (retirement) and Cam Jurgens (trade) on the offensive line. Where are they supposed to get any sort of production from? Everything says the Panthers should win this game, so naturally, they could find a way to lose it. But I think we've seen this year that these aren't the same old Panthers, and this is the sort of statement win they've been building to and getting more of over the last two seasons. Preston Palm: Panthers 27, Eagles 19 This feels like a trap game spot for the Panthers. Even with no Jalen Hurts, no Saquon Barkley, and a suspect offensive line, the Eagles are going to play Carolina close. That said, if the offense maintains the rhythm it’s had almost all season, then Carolina's defense should be able to do just enough against backup personnel. Chicago’s third-string QB diced this Philadelphia defense up, so there's no reason Young can't do the same. After escaping with wins against the Commanders and Titans to open the season, the Eagles have lost to the Bears, Rams, and Jaguars. This past week’s loss in London was particularly painful as the Eagles took a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left on the clock before Jacksonville’s kick return and a 57-yard field goal with time expiring. Things went from bad to worse on Thursday with news that Jalen Hurts will be out due to a blood clot. On the flip side, the Panthers are back in action after a bye week and 32-26 upset win against the Lions in their last game. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 6 matchup with a final score prediction. Panthers vs. Eagles Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers -3.5 (-110) Eagles +3.5 (-110) Panthers: -185 38.5 (Over -108/Under -112) Line Movement: The spread has moved quite a bit since the odds opened for this game. The Eagles are now +3.5 after opening as -1.5 favorites, largely due to the Jalen Hurts injury news. The total has plummeted from 43.5 to 38.5 Panthers vs. Eagles Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: There are very few teams I think the Eagles should be favored against, and the Panthers coming off a BYE week isn't one of them. Not only have the offensive injuries racked up in a major way for Philadelphia, but its numbers continue to be amongst the worst in the NFL. The Eagles are 29th in EPA per play and 24th in opponent EPA per play, putting them in the bottom handful of teams in the entire NFL. They're also dead last in success rate and 22nd in opponent success rate. They've somehow managed to play in close games all season, but unless they fix things in a hurry, they're going to start racking up some ugly losses. Meanwhile, the Panthers' offense is a top-10 unit. They still have some issues on defense, but their offense alone makes me think they should be favored in this NFC matchup. I'll back the Panthers as underdogs on the moneyline. Pick: Panthers +104 via FanDuel The Eagles put everything they had into last week’s game and still came up short. They then had to travel back home from London while the Panthers enjoyed a week off. Carolina isn’t going to take it lightly against the Eagles. Philadelphia will be hungry, but the injuries are piling up, and that’s a bigger deal. The Panthers should win this one, and I’m surprised the total has come down by so many points. The weather doesn’t look great in Philadelphia on Sunday, but 40 points isn’t too much to ask for. Final Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Eagles 17 Claim the latest DraftKings promo code offer today. I bet on the Panthers earlier in the week when they were set as slight underdogs, but now that they're 3.5-point favorites with Hurts out, let's bet on player props instead. Panthers vs. Eagles Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chuba Hubbard OVER 72.5 Rushing Yards (-111) Tanner McKee OVER 190.5 Passing Yards (-112) Jalen Coker Anytime Touchdown (+215) Chuba Hubbard is quietly having one of the best seasons among running backs this season. He has already racked up 306 yards, averaging 5.0 yards per rush, and scoring three touchdowns. he has also added 10 receptions for 84 yards through the air. The Panthers would be smart to keep feeding him the ball, so let's see if he can reach 73+ yards on Sunday. In this week's edition of the Player Prop Countdown , I gave out Tanner McKee to go over his passing yards total as my No. 3-ranked prop for this week: I think Tanner McKee is going to surprise some people on Sunday when he gets the start over Jalen Hurts. Hurts' play has been one of the downfalls of the Eagles' offense, so someone new under center may lead to good things, especially considering how well backup quarterbacks have played in their first starts across the league so far this season. It's also worth noting that the Panthers haven't exactly been an elite defense so far this season. They rank 20th in opponent dropback EPA and 21st in opponent dropback success rate. We aren't asking much for McKee to reach 187+ yards through the air. Tetairoa McMillan has been getting all the shine for the Panthers this season, and for good reason, but Jalen Coker has just as many touchdowns as McMillan with two and is second on the team in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (222). He also has multiple touchdown passes in three of his four games this season, just the second time he's had a stretch like that in his four-year NFL career. home.headline: Eagles' Handling of Jalen Hurts' Blood Clot Diagnosis Reportedly Won't Result in NFL Discipline
home.blurb: As a result, Hurts was held out of Philadelphia's game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. A joint statement from the Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released on Monday announced Hurts would likely miss the remainder of the season after additional testing showed he had blood clots in his lungs. The Philadelphia Eagles will not face any discipline from the NFL over their handling of Jalen Hurts' injury reporting and the medical process regarding his blood clot diagnosis. Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the NFL has concluded its investigation into the situation and won't issue any discipline to the Eagles. Deion 'Praying For' Hurts 🙏 Hurts was added to Philadelphia's Week 5 injury report on Friday with what was labeled a calf injury, but he was a full participant in practice that day and played the entire game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The club announced on Oct. 15 that Hurts injured his calf when he took a cleat to the area during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The day before the Jaguars game after their flight to London and a walkthrough, he had an ultrasound that revealed a superficial blood clot in his calf. According to Jones, "Allen Sills, the NFL's chief medical doctor, arranged with Mark Gillett, the chief medical officer of the Premier League, to have Hurts seen at the Cleveland Clinic in London on Saturday night following a team walkthrough. That is where the superficial blood clot in Hurts's calf was first discovered, and the source says that the team, staff, doctors and Hurts made the determination that he could play the following day against the Jaguars." A follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday showed the blood clot in Hurts' calf had moved. The statement adds Hurts is expected to make a full recovery and he will be able to resume his NFL career when he comes off blood thinners. This season will mark the first time since entering the NFL that Hurts will miss more than two games. He appeared in 15 games as a rookie in 2020 and started at least 15 games from 2021 to '25. Tanner McKee, who got the starting nod against the Panthers, will remain the No. 1 quarterback on Sunday when the Eagles host the Dallas Cowboys. Giants in a close one. The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers. As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Steelers 24, Bucs 20 The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers. I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays. I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win. Overall Record: 3-2 James Hill, Writer: Steelers 21, Bucs 17 I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend. Overall record: 2-3 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 21, Steelers 14 So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week. Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon. Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win. Logan Robinson, Founder: Steelers 31, Bucs 24 This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh. I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season. I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter. River Wells, Editor: Steelers 24, Bucs 17 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better. The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters. On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too. The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it. Consensus: Steelers 4, Bucs 1 The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year? picks.blurb: Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Reese, Dream get even Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:13 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first victory of the season last week, but must go on a winning streak in order to make it meaningful. At 1-4, the Bucs are only 1.5 games behind the Carolina Panthers in the weak NFC South division. However, Tampa must win a few more games before it can even start thinking about making the playoffs. Luckily, the Bucs have winnable games on the schedule over the next few weeks, including a pair against division rivals. However, Tampa has the Pittsburgh Steelers on the docket next, already the Bucs' third game against an AFC North foe. The Steelers are 3-2 and have been inconsistent this season, although their offense has turned a corner after a very slow start. The Bucs are 2.5-point underdogs at home, but managed to pull off the upset against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 as 9.5-point underdogs. Beating the Steelers will qualify as an upset, but it is a very winnable game for the Bucs. Aside from a non-existent pass rush, the Bucs' defense has been very good this season. Now it must contend with a red-hot Aaron Rodgers, who has thrown for three TDs in each of Pittsburgh's last three games. Steelers' RB Jaylen Warren has also been outstanding in the last three games, rushing for 127, 93, and 101 yards. He also caught an 80-yard TD last week, and his 230 receiving yards lead the team. Tampa's run defense is second in the NFL so far, and stopping Warren is one of my five keys to a Bucs' victory , as is finally getting the pass rush to show a pulse. On offense, the Bucs have a budding star in RB Bucky Irving, who is coming off a career-best 165 rushing yards and had both a rushing and a receiving TD against Dallas. For Tampa to win, Irving must continue to be the centerpiece of the offense. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be making his third straight start while starting QB Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb. Daniels has played with the poise of a seasoned veteran and earned the first victory of his career against the Cowboys. For Tampa to win, Daniels must once again play a clean, turnover-free game. The offensive line must keep Pittsburgh's pass rush, especially T.J. Watt, away from Daniels. This game is set to be a matchup of strengths against strengths. Warren is sixth in the NFL in rushing yards and will be going up against Tampa's strong run defense. Rodgers has been great over the last three weeks, but will have to make plays against a secondary that has shut down the star WR duos of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Steelers will be without WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson in this game. If Irving can get going early, it will make life much easier for Daniels, whose ability to also make plays with his legs can be a huge factor, especially on third down. This game seems like it could go either way, with a turnover or missed kick looming large at game's end. I don't think it will be Chase McLaughlin who misses the kick, as he has been perfect this season for the Bucs. Prediction: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 22

The team announced they have signed wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to the practice squad. McCarthy spent halftime in the blue medical tent Getty Images Instead of spending halftime in the locker room, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy spent it in the medical tent after he sustained an ankle injury at the conclusion of the first half. McCarthy was starting to make his way to the locker room when he started limping and had trouble walking. He was then assisted off the field and into the blue medical tent. He did not speak to the Steelers at halftime. After the game, he revealed he had been stepped on, and that's why he had to go into the blue tent. However, he said he is feeling better. He told the media he delegated much of the halftime head coach responsibilities to assistant coach Joe Whitt Jr. Despite the injury, McCarthy returned to the sideline for the start of the second half. He has also resumed his duties as the team's offensive playcaller. According to the CBS Sports broadcast team, McCarthy twisted his ankle, but it's unclear exactly when or what caused it. McCarthy's injury capped off what was a lousy first half for the Steelers, who trailed 13-3 at the intermission. Pittsburgh committed several mental errors in the first half, including Darnell Washington's juggling of an Aaron Rodgers pass, which was ultimately picked off by A'Shawn Robinson . The pick set up the game's first score, a 43-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin . The Steelers' offense gained just 102 yards in the first half. home.headline: Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield may try to return from injury for Panthers game
home.blurb: It sounds like Mayfield could attempt to return to the lineup when the Buccaneers play at the 3-2 Carolina Panthers on Oct. 25. Bowles previously said that Mayfield would likely be sidelined for "a minimum of three weeks" due to his setback, but a subsequent report noted that the signal-caller wanted to return after just two missed games. Such a scenario didn't play out, but Ira Kaufman of the JoeBucsFan website noted on Monday that "even Baker Mayfield detractors can’t muster a sensible argument to keep him sidelined once he is healed from a dislocated right thumb" following what happened at Tampa Bay's Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon. A Tampa Bay Buccaneers side that has been without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield since he went down with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand in Week 3 fell to 1-5 on the season when it squandered a 16-3 lead en route to suffering a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Buccaneers will evaluate Baker Mayfield "during the week" ahead of Panthers game Per Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles confirmed on Monday that Mayfield is on track to practice this coming Wednesday. "He’s supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said about Mayfield. "We’re gonna take a good look at him there, and we’ll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does." U ndrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has served as Tampa Bay's temporary QB1 since the club's Week 4 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 4. While Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown to help Tampa Bay earn a stunning 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 8, he came back down to earth when he tossed a pair of interceptions and took five sacks in the Buccaneers' loss to the Steelers. Buccaneers will try to get Baker Mayfield, Jalon Daniels ready for Panthers game "Both will be in the meetings, obviously," Bowles added about Mayfield and Daniels. "Both will be in the meetings, and we’ll see how the week goes before we decide who it is." After Bowles offered his Mayfield update, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Buccaneers on Monday as three-point underdogs against the Panthers. Want more articles like this? L.A. remains near the top of the odds in the Super Bowl market, but a few injuries – and some close losses – have dropped the Rams to 2-3 and in third place in the NFC West. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to Buffalo at home, yet it’s favored by double digits in this divisional battle with Jacoby Brissett and Co. The Cardinals shocked the NFL world in Week 1, upsetting the Los Angeles Chargers, but the Chargers’ 0-5 start has taken a little away from that victory. Since then, Arizona has lost four straight games, allowing over 30 points in all of them. Plus, the team traded away former top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Houston Texans. At some point, it feels like rookie Carson Beck will get a chance under center, as the Cards are destined for a top-five pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. So, do the Rams take care of business and cover at home? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game. It’s an exciting exercise that we hope will help guide bettors on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! As the Rams look to get back over .500, they are in desperate need of a get-right game against a weak division opponent. Here’s my final score prediction for this NFC West clash in Week 6. Cardinals vs. Rams Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s betting on Arizona to cover the spread: The Rams have a glaring issue that cost them on Monday Night Football, and it's something that leads me to be cautious about betting on them to cover big spreads: their special teams. It's the worst special teams in the league and has been for the past couple of years. If they make another blunder in Week 6, it's going to tee the Cardinals up to at least cover this big point spread. The Cardinals' defense is one of the worst in the NFL, but they have enough weapons on offense that they should be able to be at least somewhat effective in this game against a Rams team on a short week. I'll take the points with Arizona. I see where MacMillan is coming from with this bet, but the Cardinals have been blown out by Seattle and Detroit this season, and their offense may struggle against a Rams defense that remains a top-five unit against the pass (fourth in EPA/Pass) in 2026. L.A.’s special teams issues are certainly worth looking at, but the Cardinals have allowed over 30 points to Detroit, the New York Giants, Seattle and San Francisco since their win over the Los Angeles Chargers. I expect this high-powered Rams attack to push 40 points in Week 6, and I’m not buying this Jacoby Brissett-led offense to put up enough points to cover on the road. Head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie's groin injury popped up after he "felt a little something" in his groin at the end of Thursday's practice. away.headline: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed
away.blurb: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB OUT For Week 6 Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, and the ailment will keep the running back sidelined for Week 6. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn't lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona's offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 6 vs Rams
home.blurb: A groin issue was tacked on to safety Budda Baker's rest designation. The safety did not practice on Friday and is listed as questionable for the weekend. Zaven Collins also did not practice with a hip issue and is questionable. The other players questionable are punter Blake Gillikin (back) and safety Kitan Crawford (ankle). The Cardinals could activate Crawford to the roster by tomorrow afternoon. After not practicing all week, the team ruled out running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and safeties Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) and Dewey Wingard (knee). Quarterback Carson Beck had a back injury that made him limited on Friday. He did not receive a game designation. Sean McVay said cornerback Trent McDuffie pulled his groin at practice on Thursday and is listed as questionable. Safety Kam Curl is also questionable with a ankle issue. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not take part in practice on Thursday as he allows his ankle to heal. It's also looking bleak for safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) to play after logging another DNP. It was another limited practice for wide receiver Devin Duvernay (ribs) and safety Kitan Crawford (ankle). While game designations will be announced on Friday, the Cardinals have until Saturday to activate Crawford to the main roster if they want him to play this weekend. The Rams practiced for the first time this week. Safety Kam Curl was limited with an ankle injury. The ankle issue continues to linger for Jeremiyah Love. While the Cardinals running back has played through the discomfort, he did not practice on Wednesday. Coach Mike LaFleur emphasized caution and rest. Safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) also did not practice ahead of the Week 6 game against the Rams. Williams would need to progress through concussion protocol to play. Kitan Crawford had his 21-day practice window opened and returned to practice after exiting Week 1 with an ankle injury. He was limited. Wide receiver/returner Devin Duvernay (ribs) was also limited. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers: NFL Week 6 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the third time in five games to begin the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs will square off against an opponent from their own division. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group. With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like. Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season. If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe. Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances. Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters. Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles. This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender. The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart. The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising. Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment. Justin Herbert and the Chargers have yet to win a game this season, going from a preseason darling to one of the worst teams in the NFL. Not only are the Chargers winless, but they have yet to cover the spread and rank in the bottom half of the league in almost every key metric. So, this isn’t a case of a tough schedule messing up L.A.’s playoff chances. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated and appear to be back in the mix for the No. 1 seed in the AFC after a six-win 2025 campaign. Kenneth Walker III has totally transformed a Kansas City offense that ranks in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play and success rate in 2026. Oddsmakers have set Mahomes and Co. as massive favorites at home in this AFC West clash, but can they cover? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game – a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! This AFC West matchup has major implications for the Chiefs as they eye the No. 1 seed in the conference, especially since they already had their bye. Let’s dive right into the odds and my score prediction for Sunday’s game. Chargers vs. Chiefs Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chargers +8.5 (-115) Chiefs -8.5 (-105) Chargers: +380 42.5 (Over -108/Under -112) The total in this matchup has dropped a point since open , but the Chiefs remain 8.5-point favorites at home against a Chargers team that has yet to get a win in 2026. Los Angeles is 0-4-1 against the spread after failing to cover against Denver in Week 5. Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s taking the OVER in this matchup: Don't look now, but the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs once again have one of the best offenses in football. They lead the league in yards per play, averaging 6.5 yards per snap, and they also rank fourth in EPA per play and fifth in offensive success rate. Led by Offensive Player of the Year favorite Kenneth Walker, they're a dangerous offense to face, and any game they're involved in shouldn't have a total in the low 40s. Unfortunately, the Chargers' offense is bad, but I continue to believe that Mike McDaniel's system is going to eventually click, and they're going to have some strong offensive outputs sooner rather than later. Now that they face an average Chiefs defense facing an 0-6 record to start the season, now could be the time that their offense comes out firing. While I don’t mind the OVER play, I think this is going to be a lopsided game, especially since Los Angeles is banged up across the board on offense. Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris have all been hurt in 2026, and the Chargers have tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve. That’s led to a terrible offense, as L.A. ranks 32nd in the NFL in EPA/Play and 28th in success rate through five weeks. As MacMillan mentioned, this Chiefs offense has been one of the best in the league, and I expect Patrick Mahomes and Co. to take care of business out of a bye week against a Chargers team that has a very slim chance of turning this season around. L.A. has yet to cover the spread in a game this season, and bettors should expect that to change on Sunday. away.headline: NFL suspends Bills safety Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Raiders
away.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, he re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn't rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. The Bills reached out to White a few weeks ago and targeted the bye week for his return. Buffalo opened up a practice squad spot by releasing cornerback A.J. Woods. ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardiner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardiner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being “inexcusable," and said he's discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills announced they're bringing back a familiar face by signing cornerback Tre'Davious White to their practice squad. The 31-year-old White returns for what would be a third stint in Buffalo, and provide the Bills secondary with some much-needed experience. home.headline: NFL suspends Bills safety Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, he re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn't rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. The Bills reached out to White a few weeks ago and targeted the bye week for his return. Buffalo opened up a practice squad spot by releasing cornerback A.J. Woods. ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardiner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardiner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being “inexcusable," and said he's discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills announced they're bringing back a familiar face by signing cornerback Tre'Davious White to their practice squad. The 31-year-old White returns for what would be a third stint in Buffalo, and provide the Bills secondary with some much-needed experience. White was selected by Buffalo in the first round of the 2017 draft, and spent his first seven seasons with the Bills before his career was derailed by injuries. See AP’s full NFL coverage here

home.blurb: Bills' Final Week 6 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Four Others Questionable to Face Raiders Skip to main content SI.COM The Buffalo Bills have ruled five players as questionable to face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. One of the 10 without a game designation is starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left the Week 5 win , and did not return, after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform. In another positive development, running back Ty Johnson, who was limited by a hamstring at the first two practices, participated in full on Friday, and he's been cleared for the Sunday game. DJ Moore, Ed Oliver return to practice Moore and Oliver both sat out the October 12 win over the Los Angeles Rams after injury incidents knocked them out of the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots. Neither player participated at practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but both returned to the field in a limited capacity on Friday, providing a glimmer of hope that they'll be available for kickoff. "They've been doing a lot on the side. They've been doing all the walkthroughs and everything. It was good to get them out here today, and just being able to move around," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady . "We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play." After being scratched in Week 5, Alford and Palmer logged limited participation all three days this week. The former is nursing a minor ankle issue that emerged against the Patriots. The latter is fighting through a shoulder injury from an October 9 practice. Both Alford and Palmer showed positive signs throughout the week, looking ready to return to game action, by multiple accounts, during media-viewing portions of practice. Sanders, who has already dealt with a knee issue and a subsequent bout with appendicitis, made his season debut on October 12. He performed well over 51 defensive snaps, but apparently came out of the overtime win bothered by a shoulder. He progressed to full participation at Friday's practice, but remains questionable to play. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious. New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers. Cowboys vs. Packers prediction Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams . However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. picks.blurb: Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Cowboys vs. Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Sunday’s action in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season closes out with an exciting rivalry matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers, two teams fighting to get into the playoff picture in the NFC. Green Bay is coming off a huge win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5, riding 367 passing yards and two scores from Jordan Love to a second straight victory. The Pack are now 3-2 this season, but they haven’t been impressive on offense for most of the year. Meanwhile, Dallas was shockingly upset in Week 5, losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and backup quarterback Jalon Daniels on Thursday Night Football. Dallas has the No. 32 defense in the league in EPA/Play, success rate and yards per play allowed, putting a ton of pressure on Dak Prescott and Co. to score on just about every possession. The result for Sunday’s game? A total in the 50s and a very close spread between two teams that have some work to do if they want to make the postseason in the NFC. So, how should we bet on it? All week long, the SI Betting team has made picks for this game, including several player prop selections and anytime touchdown scorer props. To give our readers a quick primer for this game, I’ve compiled all of our top picks into one story ahead of Sunday night’s Cowboys vs. Packers showdown. Let’s dive in! Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Cowboys vs. Packers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers OVER 52.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan George Pickens Anytime TD (+150) – Peter Dewey Christian Watson OVER 71.5 Receiving Yards (-115) – Iain MacMillan Jordan Love OVER 271.5 Passing Yards (-113) – Peter Dewey Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the OVER on Sunday night: My strategy for the Cowboys this season is fairly straightforward. If they're favored, bet against them; if they're getting points, take them, if it's close to a pick'em bet the OVER. Their defense is too bad to lay points on them, but their offense is too good to ever underestimate them. That's why, in this week's coin-flip game against the Packers, I'm going to bet the OVER, especially considering the Packers have a similar issue. The two defenses in this game rank 24th and 32nd in opponent success rate, with the Cowboys also ranking 32nd in opponent EPA per play. Let's sit back and root for points on Sunday Night Football. George Pickens had by far his best game of the 2026 season in Week 5, catching nine of his 13 targets for 130 yards and a score. It was the first time in 2026 that Pickens found the end zone, but I think he’s a little undervalued at this price in a potential shootout in Week 6. CeeDee Lamb was banged up at the end of Dallas’ Week 5 loss, and Pickens could take on a lead role for a Cowboys offense that is No. 5 in EPA/Play and No. 4 in total passing yards. Last season, Pickens found the end zone nine times, and he could be due for some positive regression in Week 6 and beyond. MacMillan shares his favorite prop bets of the week in his Player Prop Countdown , and Watson is the No. 4 player in Week 6: Christian Watson has had a breakout season so far in 2026. He enters Week 6 ranking fifth in the NFL in receiving yards, racking up 474 yards for 94.8 per game. Now, he and the Packers get to face arguably the worst defense in the entire league. The Cowboys have given up 8.1 yards per pass attempt, and they also rank last in both opponent dropback EPA and opponent dropback success rate. There couldn't be a better matchup for Jordan Love in Week 6. The Packers quarterback has led the team to the third-most passing yards in the NFL this season, and now he’s taking on Green Bay defense that is last in the NFL in EPA/Play, success rate, EPA/Pass and yards per play allowed. Love has over 271.5 passing yards in three games this season (all over 300 yards), and he already has multiple games with over 40 pass attempts. away.blurb: This is Trask's return to the NFL. Sam Howell remains the backup behind the starter. Howell beat out Milton in the preseason quarterback battle, and nothing about the Trask signing changes that. The Cowboys drafted Carson out of Wake Forest in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. The hope was that he would bring flexibility to the cornerback room, with the versatility to play both inside and outside. It never worked out. Carson never looked like the player Dallas thought it was getting out of college. When he did play, it was mostly out of necessity, and a rough preseason in August didn't help his case. One special teams standout is finally getting his reward. The Dallas Cowboys made multiple roster moves ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles. The changes touch both the 53-man roster and the practice squad, and they include a quarterback. At 2-4, Dallas can't afford to waste a roster spot right now. These moves reflect that, from depth at quarterback to rewarding a core special teamer. Cowboys add Kyle Trask to the practice squad The Cowboys are signing quarterback Kyle Trask to the practice squad. Dallas carried three quarterbacks until the Eagles poached Joe Milton off the practice squad last week. Trask now fills the spot Milton left behind. You might remember Trask from his college days with the Florida Gators. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft. He has since spent time with the Atlanta Falcons and the Carolina Panthers, and Carolina released him as part of its final roster cuts before the regular season. Don't expect him to push for QB2 snaps, though. Trask has appeared in seven games in his NFL career and attempted only 11 passes across those appearances. Despite his second-round pedigree, he has never really gotten a chance to play in a major way. He has spent most of his career as a backup. For the Cowboys, this move is about depth. They like to carry three quarterbacks, and signing Trask gives them a 28-year-old option in case it's ever needed. Juanyeh Thomas earns a spot on the 53-man roster Here's the move that might matter most on Sundays (or Monday, in this case). Dallas is signing Juanyeh Thomas to the 53-man roster after elevating him from the practice squad three consecutive times. Teams can only lean on elevations for so long, and Thomas has made the decision an easy one. He has become a core special teamer.
