Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook. While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White , Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football. The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL . San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards. Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa , but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night. When the 49ers have the ball San Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league. Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are. Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game. Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards. The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't. I picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense. The San Francisco 49ers and Brock Purdy are looking to keep their undefeated season going when they host the Washington Commanders and former No. 2 overall pick Jayden Daniels. San Francisco upset the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, and it has one of the best offenses in the league during this perfect 5-0 start. Purdy is gaining some MVP buzz, and the 49ers have battled through several major injuries to sit atop the NFC standings. Meanwhile, Washington tied the New York Giants in Week 5 after a late-game blunder led to the clock expiring on the team – in field goal range – in overtime. Daniels and the Commanders are now just 1-3-1 this season (0-2-1 when Daniels plays), and they need as many wins as they can get to remain in the mix to win the NFC East. The 49ers are considerable favorites in this game, and the total is one of the highest of the week at 50.5. In the leadup to this game, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player props selections and much more to help bettors get the most out of this matchup. I’ve decided to compile some of our favorite plays all into one spot ahead of Monday’s action. Here’s a breakdown of each of these bets – and their latest odds in the Commanders vs. 49ers matchup. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Commanders vs. 49ers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook San Francisco 49ers -7.5 (-110) vs. Washington Commanders – Iain MacMillan Brock Purdy OVER 2.5 Passing Touchdowns (+146) – Peter Dewey Jayden Daniels OVER 36.5 Rushing Yards (-109) – Peter Dewey Mike Evans Anytime TD (-140) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . In Week 6, he’s taking the 49ers to cover at home: The only argument you can make to bet on the Commanders in this game, and it's not necessarily one that I'd disagree with, is that so many things have gone right for the 49ers through the first five weeks that they're bound to have a game where things go wrong. If that happens, and if Jayden Daniels can drag the Commanders' offense down the field enough, maybe Washington can cover this spread. With that being said, that's not enough for me to take the Commanders here, and considering I expect the line to shift even more towards San Francisco this week, I'll take them at -7.5 while I still can. There's a strong argument to be made that the 49ers are the best team in the NFL. They're second in net yards per play (+1.7), second in EPA per play, first in success rate, fourth in opponent EPA per play, and eighth in opponent success rate. They're well-balanced on both sides of the ball, and now they get to host a bad Commanders team in a prime time slot. There's a chance this game gets ugly. Brock Purdy has thrown at least two scores in every game this season, and he has two games with three or more touchdown passes (against the Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals). Washington has given up the most touchdown passes in the league (14) through five weeks, and Jameis Winston torched this secondary in the second half of Week 5. Overall, the Commanders are 23rd in EPA/Pass and 29th in passing yards allowed in 2026. This is a dream matchup for Purdy, who has thrown the ball just over 28 times per game for the offense that is No. 1 in success rate and No. 2 in EPA/Play this season. At +146, I think this prop is worth a shot against one of the worst pass defenses in the NFL. Jayden Daniels has only played in three games this season, but the Commanders quarterback has 203 rushing yards and two scores. Now, 103 of those yards came in Week 5 against the New York Giants, but Daniels has cleared this rushing yards total twice, picking up over 60 yards in two of his games. The 49ers’ defense is a top-five unit in EPA/Rush, so I expect plenty of dropbacks for Daniels on Monday night. away.headline: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin out for season with knee injury
away.blurb: The incident took place during the opening quarter of the Week 6 matchup while McLaurin was running a route against 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir. The injury appeared to occur without any physical contact from an opponent; as McLaurin moved toward the sideline, his left knee buckled, causing him to collapse in visible pain. He was immediately ruled out for the remainder of the contest. The Washington Commanders have confirmed that veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin will miss the remainder of the season due to a severe knee injury. The injury occurred during the first quarter of Monday night’s 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, forcing the receiver to be carted off the field after receiving an air cast on his leg. Following the game, medical examinations confirmed the severity of the situation. An MRI conducted on Tuesday revealed that McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon. According to reports from NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the 31-year-old receiver is scheduled to undergo surgery to repair the damage, effectively ending his campaign. Injury Details and Team Response Commanders head coach Dan Quinn had expressed significant concern regarding the receiver's status immediately following the game. Acknowledging the gravity of the situation, Quinn noted that there was a clear fear that the injury would prove to be substantial. Rapoport later confirmed the diagnosis on social media, describing it as a brutal setback for the player and noting that he faces a lengthy recovery process. Impact on the Commanders Offense McLaurin’s absence marks a notable loss for the Washington offense. Despite missing the team's Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts due to a previous hamstring issue, he had recorded 15 receptions for 230 yards and one touchdown during the current season. A third-round draft pick in 2019, McLaurin has spent his entire professional career with the Washington franchise. The Commanders are currently entering a bye week, providing the team time to adjust their roster and offensive strategy before returning to competition. They are scheduled to face the Philadelphia Eagles on November 1. The team has not yet provided further details on potential roster moves to address the vacancy left by the veteran receiver. Stay updated with the latest and breaking news on Times World.

away.headline: Commanders star wide receiver Terry McLaurin out for season with patellar tendon injury, coach says
away.blurb: Star wide receiver Terry McLaurin is out for the remainder of the season with a torn left patellar tendon, coach Dan Quinn announced Tuesday. McLaurin will undergo surgery to repair the injury. Original article source: Commanders star wide receiver Terry McLaurin out for season with patellar tendon injury, coach says The reeling Washington Commanders are going to be without one of their biggest offensive weapons. "Man, he brings a lot on and off the field," Quinn said of McLaurin while speaking to reporters. "I felt him in so many unique ways this season from training camp to in-season. For him to even start the game like he did was significant." The 31-year-old suffered the injury while running a route in the first quarter of the Commanders’ 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night. He was carted off the field with an air cast on his left leg. The two-time Pro Bowler has spent his entire eight-year career with the Commanders. In five games this season, he had 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown. Over his career, he has 513 catches for 7,191 yards and 42 touchdowns. Before the 2025 season, McLaurin signed a three-year, $96 million contract extension after a lengthy holdout. The deal runs through the 2028 season. Next season, he is owed $23.3 million, including $5.35 million guaranteed for injury if he isn't healthy by April 1. That provision could potentially cloud his future with the team. In McLaurin’s absence, Stefon Diggs, rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams and tight end Chig Okonkwo could see more targets from quarterback Jayden Daniels. The Commanders are 1-4-1 and sit in last place in the NFC East. They have a bye in Week 7. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

away.headline: 49ers Week 6 injury report vs. Commanders: WRs to target in fantasy football with Mike Evans banged up
away.blurb: Head coach Kyle Shanahan is doing anything but breathing easy at this point. The 49ers have suffered a slew of injuries that have impacted them throughout the season, and there is no let up as they prepare for the Commanders. They have gotten a dynamic performance from the QB-RB-WR trio of Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans to this point in the season, but Evans is battered and bruised in his first season with the 49ers. He is listed as questionable for the Week 6 Monday night game. He has been battling bruised ribs and now he also has an Achilles issue that kept him out of practice Friday. It would be a major blow if the 49ers did not have him in the lineup against the Commanders. While Shanahan and Purdy have to be prepared for that possibility and have alternatives in mind, Evans will fight to remain in the lineup. “We all know what he’s been playing through, the immense pain that he has every single play,” said 49ers center Jake Brendel , per Matt Barrows of The Athletic . “He still goes out there and does his very best to get a completion for us. It’s fantastic.” Brandin Cooks will be the Niners' primary deep threat in this game, and if Evans can't play or is severely limited, he will become their No. 1 receiver. Cooks has only played in 2 games this season and his numbers are not significant. He has caught just 3-7-1, but that does not mean he would struggle in this game. Cooks is a 13-year veteran receiver with the tools and the know-how to make a key contribution. 49ers Week 6 injury report vs. Commanders: WRs to target in fantasy football with Mike Evans banged up NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes Mike Evans is battling broken ribs and Achilles problem with Niners, but he could play vs. Commanders despite injury status. home.headline: Commanders-49ers injury report: Stefon Diggs and Mike Evans remain key questions
home.blurb: Washington wide receiver Stefon Diggs is listed as questionable with a hamstring injury after practicing on a limited basis. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is out with a groin injury, as are quarterback Marcus Mariota, defensive end Charles Omenihu and linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste. San Francisco will be without two of its biggest names. Defensive end Nick Bosa is out with a calf injury, and wide receiver Deebo Samuel is sidelined with a hamstring issue. Four other 49ers, Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, Gracen Halton and Mykel Williams, are among those listed as questionable. The injury list also complicates the backfield. With Croskey-Merritt ruled out, Washington will have to adjust its workload at running back. The team’s final inactive list will provide the clearest picture of who is available closer to kickoff. home.headline: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers
home.blurb: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers Skip to main content SI.COM The Washington Commanders' final injury report lists a baker's dozen of players out or questionable, sure to create an availability problem for Washington facing the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Four players are officially listed as out: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee) , and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle). All four players missed practice all week. Nine additional players are also listed as questionable, including Stefon Diggs, Javon Kinlaw, and three safeties. Of the three safeties, Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice but were upgraded to limited; Nick Cross (illness) was a full participant all three days but is still questionable. All three players missed last week's game against New York . Quan Martin improved from limited on Thursday to full participation on Friday and Saturday, with no game designation. Stefon Diggs' return is possible; he's officially listed as questionable. He went from missing Thursday's practice to limited on both Friday and Saturday. Terry McLaurin has no game designation after being limited Thursday and Saturday and sitting out Friday with a hamstring/rest designation. Treylon Burks was also limited all three days but has no game designation. Getting Diggs back would give Jayden Daniels another option in the passing game after playing without him against the Giants. The Commanders will also be without Croskey-Merritt in the backfield , but they should have options. Austin Ekeler was limited all week with a chest injury, while Rachaad White went from full participation Thursday to limited Friday and Saturday. Neither received a game designation. Jeremy McNichols was a full participant all three days but remains questionable with a quad injury. He would also need to be activated from injured reserve before he can play Monday. UPDATE: McNichols, Trey Amos, and Jordan Magee were activated Monday afternoon before the game. Washington Commanders PR Washington's defensive front is another area to watch with Omenihu and Jean-Baptiste both out. Kinlaw fully participated Thursday, missed Friday's practice, and returned Saturday on a limited basis. He's questionable with ankle and knee injuries. K'Lavon Chaisson, meanwhile, returned to full participation Saturday after sitting out Friday and has no game designation. There are still a few roster decisions to make before Monday night. Trey Amos (ankle) and Jordan Magee (hamstring) are both questionable and, like McNichols, remain in their 21-day practice windows. Neither can play until they are activated from their respective reserve lists. Lucas Patrick is also questionable with an illness despite returning to full participation Saturday. Diggs currently sits with totals at a modest 42.5 receiving yards and 4.5 receptions. If he is hindered or sits out, expect a condensed target tree directly benefiting Terry McLaurin. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (RB) – Out The backfield depth takes a hit with Jacory Croskey-Merritt missing this duel due to a groin injury. His absence should solidify the ground and pound workload for Rachaad White. Bettors have already taken notice. White’s rushing yards total skyrocketed from an opening number of 21.5 up to 46.5, showing sharp money hammering the over. If he is cleared to play, he steps into an extremely favorable volume situation. San Francisco already ruled out Demarcus Robinson. In three games Robinson missed this season, Evans capitalized by averaging a robust 74 receiving yards. The best available market sets Evans' receiving yards prop at 63.5 (Over -112). Without Samuel to stretch the field horizontally, the offense will likely condense around remaining healthy targets like George Kittle.
